A common path is to earn vocational or associate-level education in statistics, mathematics, business, or economics, enter a statistical role as an assistant, master Excel and statistical software, independently handle cleaning and reports, and transition into statistical analysis or another data role.
This occupation suits meticulous people who can sit for long periods and persist with spreadsheets. If you treat matching numbers as a nonnegotiable requirement, you can thrive in this field.

Statistical Assistants help collect, enter, and clean data, verify samples and records using consistent definitions, calculate descriptive statistics and basic reports, identify outliers, and provide accurate, reliable source data for statistical analysis and decision-making.

paragraphs: Start the day by receiving data requirements and definitions. Enter questionnaire and administrative data into the system and check every column for missing values and outliers. Clean data according to consistent rules and request verification for suspicious values. Run descriptive statistics, produce foundational tables, and create basic charts. Before leaving, archive the files and send them to analysts with anomalies clearly marked for review.

In short, they turn disorganized numbers into usable foundational tables. Their work includes entering data, verifying definitions, cleaning messy values, calculating descriptive statistics, creating basic charts, archiving, and reviewing. They use both hands and eyes and form the foundation of data work.

Employment is projected to decline to 6,300 by 2034, a net decrease of about 200 jobs, with about 800 openings each year on average. The median annual wage in 2026 was about $51,400 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace statistical assistants, but it will take over data entry and cleaning. Scripts and AI automatically clean messy data, shifting assistants from entering numbers toward enforcing definitions, identifying anomalies, reviewing work, and conducting quality checks.
